Issues.Title: [release/6.0] Modernise Linux CI containers and native compiler discovery
Issues.Body:
Backport of dotnet/machinelearning#7868 to `release/6.0`.

Replace the Ubuntu 18.04 build environments with newer published images to address Azure Pipelines task-runner compatibility, without disabling Node.js EOL restrictions.

- Use `ubuntu-22.04-mlnet` for Ubuntu x64 PR validation and nightly builds.
- Use dotnet/runtime release/8.0's `azurelinux-3.0-net8.0-cross-arm` and `cross-arm64` images for PR and official ARM builds, with `LDFLAGS=-fuse-ld=lld` to select the bundled LLVM linker.
- Add Clang 14 discovery while preserving existing compiler preferences.
- Move Linux nightly hosted agents to Ubuntu 22.04 and update the associated template conditions.
- Document the container choices and native compatibility constraints.

The CentOS Stream 8 build images, including the official x64 native-package build, are unchanged to avoid silently raising the system-library requirements of shipped native assets.

Issues.Title: Disable copy hard links in code coverage builds
Issues.Body:
Disable copy hard links for coverage builds to keep Coverlet's instrumented assemblies and PDBs separate from the original build outputs.

The coverage pipeline already omitted `CreateHardLinksForCopyLocalIfPossible=True`, but still unconditionally enabled `CreateHardLinksForCopyFilesToOutputDirectoryIfPossible=True`. This can make the `obj` and `bin` PDB paths refer to the same underlying file.

Coverlet rewrites assemblies and PDBs during instrumentation. Instrumenting one project's output can therefore lock the original PDB while another project reads it, a likely cause of the recurring file-access failures.

## Changes

- Explicitly set both copy hard-link options to `False` for coverage builds.
- Preserve the existing build command and hard-link settings for non-coverage jobs.
- Leave native/publish linking and test parallelism unchanged.

The trade-off is increased disk usage and copy I/O in the coverage job, without serialising test execution.

Fixes #7417

Issues.Title: Make Word.MergeAll sub-quadratic
Issues.Body:
The current implementation of `Word.MergeAll` uses `Vec<T>.Remove()` to remove symbols from the list:

https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/81310b23aeee0cc12720edde8794e3cc94afef3e/src/Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers/Model/Word.cs#L187-L194

Based on data I found, it seems it's common that around 75 % of symbols are removed here (though the data conflates multiple steps, so it could be not fully relevant). This makes the method quadratic, likely significantly affecting its performance.

We should consider improving that. (This won't make the method linear, since the use of `PriorityQueue<T>` leads to at least O(n log n).)

Issues.Title: Maximize AutoML log-loss reduction
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7839.

`MultiClassMetricManager` currently minimizes `LogLossReduction`, so AutoML prefers a lower reduction even though a higher value is better. Mark it as a maximizing metric, consistent with the existing multiclass metrics agent.

Add deterministic coverage through `SetMulticlassClassificationMetric`: verify all five optimization directions, then use three fixed trial scores to check that LogLossReduction selects the highest score while LogLoss selects the lowest. The seven new cases produce two failures before the fix and all pass afterward. No public API or TopKAccuracy evaluation changes are included.

Validation on Windows x64, Release/net8.0:
- New metric direction and trial-selection cases: 7 passed.
- Existing `MetricsAgentsTests`: 13 passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The full repository build was not validated locally: the machine lacks the required Spectre C++ libraries, and pretrained-image downloads stalled. For the focused managed tests, native dependencies were built locally with Spectre mitigation disabled and unused image downloads were skipped with a local MSBuild import. No build configuration changes are included in this PR.

Issues.Title: Fix native-library test discovery and oneDAL dependency copying
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Fix native-library availability checks on modern .NET using the runtime's assembly-aware loader, avoiding false Linux skips caused by the legacy `libdl` import and distro-specific RID probing. Retain the .NET Framework fallback, honor `NUGET_PACKAGES`, and resolve dependencies beside explicitly loaded Windows DLLs.
- Reuse the oneDAL/TBB dependency list in `Native.proj` for native staging, packaging, and test/build-publish copying. Add native-loading regression tests while preserving architecture and macOS exclusions.
- Isolate the oneDAL FastForest estimator test with RemoteExecutor. Select the backend before `MLContext`'s static initialization, put the test assembly directory on the child's native search path, and verify native oneDAL execution and model accuracy without leaking backend selection into later tests.
- Quarantine the two affected SymSGD estimator tests on Linux ARM32 for active issue #7837.
- Use the repository's xUnit configuration through Arcade's supported override, avoiding duplicate `xunit.runner.json` files during .NET Framework publishing. Clarify native-dependent test skip messages in a separate commit.

Native-loading failures also affect conditional trainer coverage inside ONNX conversion tests, not only tests reported as skipped.

## Remaining CI issues

The preceding CI run also exposed Linux TensorFlow process kills consistent with the memory-pressure investigation in #7836, AutoML flowers-data contention tracked in #7393, and the coverage PDB-locking issue #7417. These are not fixed by this PR; the updated CI runs will verify the oneDAL and SymSGD changes.

Issues.Title: SentencePieceTokenizer (Unigram) emits one <unk> per unknown character — SentencePiece merges a run of unknown characters into one <unk>
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`SentencePieceTokenizer.Create(stream)` on a SentencePiece **Unigram** model returns one `<unk>` id for **every character** the vocabulary lacks. The reference implementation (google/sentencepiece `unigram_model.cc`, "merges continuous run of unknown pieces") and HF `tokenizers` return a **single** `<unk>` for a run of such characters. A model trained with SentencePiece therefore receives different ids from .NET than it was trained on.

## Repro (Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 2.0.1, net10.0, osx-arm64)

1. Train a small Unigram model on a few Korean/English sentences that contain no Latin capitals:
   ```python
   spm.SentencePieceTrainer.train(input=corpus, model_type="unigram", vocab_size=80,
       normalization_rule_name="nmt_nfkc", unk_id=0, bos_id=1, eos_id=2, pad_id=-1)
   ```
2. Encode `"ＡＢＣ 전각 ①"` (NFKC → `ABC …`, three characters absent from the vocabulary):
   - sentencepiece (Python), HF `XLMRobertaTokenizer` and `XLMRobertaTokenizerFast`: `▁ <unk> ▁ <unk> ▁ <unk>` — one `<unk>` per run.
   - `SentencePieceTokenizer.EncodeToIds(text, addBeginningOfSentence: false, addEndOfSentence: false)`: `▁ <unk> <unk> <unk> ▁ <unk> <unk> ▁ <unk> <unk>` — one per character.
3. Same for `"처음 보는 글자 魑魅 😀"`: each unseen word becomes N `<unk>` instead of 1.

With a large vocabulary (XLM-RoBERTa's 250k `sentencepiece.bpe.model`) the two paths agreed on 12 everyday texts, because unknown runs are rare there — the difference shows on rare scripts and characters.

## Expected

`EncodeToIds` merges consecutive unknown pieces into one `<unk>`, as SentencePiece's Unigram encoder does. (The BPE model path may be worth checking for the same behaviour.)

## Workaround

Collapsing consecutive `UnknownId` entries after `EncodeToIds`. With that, a sentence encoder's vectors match sentence-transformers to cosine 1.000000 on 14 texts.

Issues.Title: TorchSharp text trainers (TextClassification, SentenceSimilarity, NER, QA) drop every input character above U+00FF — non-Latin text reaches the model as nothing
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The tokenizer every NAS-BERT / RoBERTa trainer in `Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp` builds (`TokenizerExtensions.GetInstance(IChannel)` — an `EnglishRobertaTokenizer` created with unsupported characters filtered) removes every input character above U+00FF **on encode**, before BPE. No `<unk>` id is produced; the characters vanish silently, so nothing during training reports it. Affected: `TextClassificationTrainer`, `SentenceSimilarityTrainer`, `NerTrainer`, `QATrainer`.

#7749 covers the decode side of the same filter (QA answers); this is the input side.

## Observed (Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp 0.23.1)

```
"음악을 들으면서"            -> tokens [Ġ]                       decode " "
"2026년 10월 25일 오전 9시"  -> [20 | 26 | Ġ10 | Ġ25 | Ġ | Ġ9]   decode "2026 10 25  9"
"Привет мир"                -> [Ġ]
"日本語のテキスト"            -> []
"café naïve résumé"         -> kept whole
```

A character-by-character check over U+0021–U+2FFF: a character is kept exactly when it is ≤ U+00FF.

## Impact

On Korean news, dialogue and sentence corpora, 82–89% of non-space characters (73–81% of words) are removed before the model sees them. Text classification, sentence similarity and NER then train on the digits, Latin letters and punctuation that are left, and report ordinary-looking metrics.

## Repro

```csharp
var ext = typeof(Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp.NasBert.NerTrainer).Assembly
    .GetType("Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp.Extensions.TokenizerExtensions");
using var ch = ((IHostEnvironment)new MLContext()).Register("t").Start("t");
var tok = (Tokenizer)ext.GetMethod("GetInstance",
        BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Public)
    .Invoke(null, new object[] { ch });
tok.Decode(tok.EncodeToIds("음악을 들으면서")); // " "
```

## Expected

Either byte-level encoding of characters outside Latin-1 (what GPT-2/RoBERTa byte-level BPE does by design), or an explicit error/warning when input text loses characters — plus documentation that these trainers are Latin-1-only until then.

Related: #7749

Issues.Title: Throw ArgumentNullException from DataFrame binary operators when the DataFrame is null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #5677

The scalar operators on `DataFrame` (`df + 1`, `1 + df`, `df << 1`, etc.) call straight into the instance method, so passing a null `DataFrame` throws a `NullReferenceException` from inside the library. As suggested in the triage comment, these now throw `ArgumentNullException` with `ParamName` set to `df`.

The `bool` overload mentioned in the issue no longer exists, since `bool` is excluded from the numeric operators, but every other operator overload had the same problem.

Changes:
- `DataFrame.BinaryOperators.tt`: add a null check on `df` to the three operator templates (scalar, reverse scalar and shift).
- `DataFrame.BinaryOperators.cs`: the matching change in the generated file, applied to all 112 operators. The only differences from the existing file are the added checks.
- New test `TestBinaryOperatorsWithNullDataFrame` covers the arithmetic, reverse and shift operators with a null `DataFrame`.

No public API is added or changed. Only the exception type thrown for a null argument is different.

Testing:
- Before the fix, the new test failed with `NullReferenceException`. After the fix, it passes.
- `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests` (net8.0, macOS arm64): 1779 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` on the changed files: clean.
